quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, your chance of dying in a crash increases. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can increase the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs can make both substances more powerful. For example, one drink taken with a cold medicine might affect you as much as several drinks taken alone.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, even if the flagger says something different.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if there was no construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Slow down and follow instructions when a flagger, sign, or police officer directs you. Not obeying is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Your current roadway ends ahead.
You must bear either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a Y intersection ahead. You must turn either right or left.

questions.question: If involved in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: After an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off engines in wrecked vehicles.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to check if another car is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to see if anyone is in your blind spot.

questions.question: When driving on major highways:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. To avoid highway hypnosis, do not stare at any one thing for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It has no effect on judgment but it harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol damages your ability to drive safely. It slows your reaction time, makes it harder to see clearly, and affects your sense of speed and distance. It also lowers your caution and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are usually not important.
Are only found in construction zones.
Provide information for drivers.
Are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers important information. They help you position your vehicle correctly, show safe passing areas, and warn you of upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the crossing guard says something different.
Assume the guard is not supposed to direct traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a crossing guard, sign, or police officer in a school zone. Be ready to slow down or stop. Drive carefully around children.

questions.question: How should drivers use the gas pedal?

options.text: Gradually and smoothly
As quickly as possible
By tapping it lightly
Any way that feels right to you

questions.explanation: Press the gas pedal slowly and smoothly. Use the top of your foot on the gas and your heel on the floor. Pressing too fast can make your wheels spin or cause your car to slide, especially on wet roads.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
The road you are on meets a divided highway.
You are driving over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road you are on meets a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guard rail.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water and puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid when you turn. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive with care.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry:

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Move away from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, move away from them physically and mentally. Avoid eye contact and hand gestures that could anger them. Slow down, change lanes, or do whatever is safe to stay out of danger.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Make no driving errors.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their cars.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:

options.text: Reduce the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
Increase the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
Help cure an illness.
Improve your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after using alcohol or drugs alone, and even more dangerous when combined.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you leave your car, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: When stopped by police, what documents must you show?

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of vehicle registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must carry your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must show all three documents when stopped by police.

questions.question: Is smoking while driving a distraction?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving.
No, it helps you stay alert.
Yes, it is a distraction.
No, it is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This creates a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Slow down and look for a train. Be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If possible, move it out of traffic. Call police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles to arrive.
